summary: FP8 KV-cache startup diagnostics now use provenance recorded by BaseKVCacheMethod during real attention-layer post-load processing. Fully calibrated baked scales, including legitimate 1.0 values, no longer trigger the fallback warning; absent and partially missing per-layer scales still warn. Legacy external JSON scales are synchronized to the k_scale_float/v_scale_float fields consumed by attention backends.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before regression on the recorded base: baked checkpoint scales still emitted the false fallback warning, and partial calibration was not reported with layer counts. Raw output: reports/j-8c9af2124bd2/raw/regression-before.txt

Eight CPU tests passed, covering legacy external JSON scales, baked per-layer scales, an exact calibrated 1.0, absent scales, partially missing layer scales, runtime k_scale_float/v_scale_float values, and compressed-tensors KV method selection. Raw output: reports/j-8c9af2124bd2/raw/regression-after.txt

On one AMD Instinct MI350X with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2/HIP 7.2.26015, actual RadixAttention layers produced calibrated 0.028/0.012, missing-scale fallback 1.0/1.0, and calibrated 1.0/1.0 runtime values with correct provenance. Values were independently compared with device float32 tensors. Raw output: reports/j-8c9af2124bd2/raw/rocm-kv-scale-contract.txt
All applicable repository formatting, lint, safety, and CI-registration hooks passed. Raw output: reports/j-8c9af2124bd2/raw/pre-commit.txt

remaining_limitations: No GB10 hardware was used; the source GB10 result is treated only as historical evidence.

No model-weight serving run was performed. Validation targets the device-independent loader/attention-layer contract and its supported ROCm execution, not model semantic accuracy or a distributed workload.
No native source changed; the prepared environment reports native=null, so a native rebuild was neither required nor performed.
